title: The Mystery Feely Bag: Parent Guide
endLine: Touch finds shape, texture and cold, but not color.

scenes.tts: Can you tell what something is without looking? A pillowcase and a few everyday objects let your child find out what skin can sense.
scenes.caption: Can you tell what something is without looking? A pillowcase and a few everyday objects let your child find out what skin can sense.
scenes.visual: Warm schematic table seen from the front, filling most of the frame. A plain pillowcase sits in the middle with soft lumps inside. A drawn child's hand slides into the opening. Large high-contrast text: 'What is it?' No photos of real children.
scenes.narration: Can you tell what something is without looking? A pillowcase and a few everyday objects let your child find out what skin can sense.

scenes.visual: Same table and pillowcase. The title 'The Mystery Feely Bag' appears above it while the cloth shifts slightly.

scenes.tts: The bag takes sight away, so touch has to do the job alone. Your child practices describing what they feel, making a guess, and checking it with their eyes. It takes about twenty-five minutes.
scenes.caption: The bag takes sight away, so touch has to do the job alone. Your child practices describing what they feel, making a guess, and checking it with their eyes. It takes about twenty-five minutes.
scenes.visual: Same table. Three short labels appear one by one beside the bag: 'Describe', 'Guess', 'Check'. A small clock icon reads '25 minutes'.
scenes.narration: The bag takes sight away, so touch has to do the job alone. Your child practices describing what they feel, making a guess, and checking it with their eyes. It takes about twenty-five minutes.

scenes.tts: You need a pillowcase and eight to ten objects with different textures. Think of a pinecone, a large smooth stone, a new sponge, a wool mitten, and an orange. Keep a metal spoon, a wooden spoon, and a spoon from the fridge aside.
scenes.caption: You need a pillowcase and eight to ten objects with different textures. Think of a pinecone, a large smooth stone, a new sponge, a wool mitten, and an orange. Keep a metal spoon, a wooden spoon, and a spoon from the fridge aside.
scenes.visual: Friendly drawn objects settle on the table above the bag, at most six at once: pinecone, smooth stone, sponge, wool mitten, orange, wooden block. Then three spoons slide to one side: metal, wooden, and a second metal spoon with a small fridge icon.
scenes.narration: You need a pillowcase and eight to ten objects with different textures. Think of a pinecone, a large smooth stone, a new sponge, a wool mitten, and an orange. Keep a metal spoon, a wooden spoon, and a spoon from the fridge aside.

scenes.tts: Stay with your child throughout. Pack and check the objects yourself. Even when squeezed, they should be too big for a toilet paper tube. Skip anything sharp, hot, frozen, breakable, alive, or with loose parts. Keep all bag objects out of mouths.
scenes.caption: Stay with your child throughout. Pack and check the objects yourself. Even when squeezed, they should be too big for a toilet paper tube. Skip anything sharp, hot, frozen, breakable, alive, or with loose parts. Keep all bag objects out of mouths.
scenes.visual: On the same table, an adult hand checks each object against a toilet paper tube, squeezing the sponge and flattening the mitten first. A marble drops through and gets an X. Show the adult checking a pinecone for loose scales and prickly tips before packing the bag out of the child's sight.
scenes.narration: Stay with your child throughout. Pack and check the objects yourself. Even when squeezed, they should be too big for a toilet paper tube. Skip anything sharp, hot, frozen, breakable, alive, or with loose parts. Keep all bag objects out of mouths.

scenes.tts: Your child puts one hand in and holds one object without looking. Say, 'Don't tell me what it is yet. Tell me what it feels like.' Ask for three describing words, like bumpy, hard, and light. Write them down.
scenes.caption: Your child puts one hand in and holds one object without looking. Say, 'Don't tell me what it is yet. Tell me what it feels like.' Ask for three describing words, like bumpy, hard, and light. Write them down.
scenes.visual: The child's hand inside the pillowcase, shown as a soft see-through cutaway, wraps around the orange. Three word cards appear one by one: 'bumpy', 'hard', 'light'. A pencil writes them on a notepad.
scenes.narration: Your child puts one hand in and holds one object without looking. Say, 'Don't tell me what it is yet. Tell me what it feels like.' Ask for three describing words, like bumpy, hard, and light. Write them down.

scenes.tts: Have your child guess, then pull out the object. Compare what they felt with what they can see. Their hand could feel the shape and bumps. Their eyes can see the color.
scenes.caption: Have your child guess, then pull out the object. Compare what they felt with what they can see. Their hand could feel the shape and bumps. Their eyes can see the color.
scenes.visual: The orange comes out of the bag. A hand icon appears beside the words 'shape' and 'bumpy'. An eye icon appears beside 'color'.
scenes.narration: Have your child guess, then pull out the object. Compare what they felt with what they can see. Their hand could feel the shape and bumps. Their eyes can see the color.

scenes.tts: Next, put the metal spoon and the wooden spoon in the bag. They have been in the same room all day.
scenes.caption: Next, put the metal spoon and the wooden spoon in the bag. They have been in the same room all day.
scenes.visual: The metal and wooden spoons slide into the bag side by side. A simple room thermometer beside them shows the same reading for both, marked 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Next, put the metal spoon and the wooden spoon in the bag. They have been in the same room all day.

scenes.tts: Both spoons are at room temperature. What do you predict? When your child feels both spoons, will one feel colder?
scenes.caption: Both spoons are at room temperature. What do you predict? When your child feels both spoons, will one feel colder?
scenes.visual: Keep the pillowcase on the table with a cutaway showing the two spoons inside. The question card reads, 'Which will feel colder?'
scenes.narration: Both spoons are at room temperature. What do you predict? When your child feels both spoons, will one feel colder?

scenes.visual: Hold the question card and the pillowcase cutaway with both spoons inside. Let the cloth shift slightly. Keep the result hidden.

scenes.tts: The metal spoon usually feels colder because it draws heat from fingers faster. Dry the fridge spoon. Hand it over with your child’s eyes closed. Ask whether it feels wet. Wipe the spoon with a dry towel and check the towel. If your child felt wetness and the towel stays dry, the cold may explain the feeling. A damp spot can come from condensation.
scenes.caption: The metal spoon usually feels colder because it draws heat from fingers faster. Dry the fridge spoon. Hand it over with your child’s eyes closed. Ask whether it feels wet. Wipe the spoon with a dry towel and check the towel. If your child felt wetness and the towel stays dry, the cold may explain the feeling. A damp spot can come from condensation.
scenes.visual: Show the child's hand feeling both spoons inside the pillowcase. Use arrows to show heat leaving the skin faster at the metal spoon. Then show the adult drying the fridge spoon before handing it over. In two alternative outcomes, show a clean towel staying dry and a clean towel picking up a damp spot.
scenes.narration: The metal spoon usually feels colder because it draws heat from fingers faster. Dry the fridge spoon. Hand it over with your child’s eyes closed. Ask whether it feels wet. Wipe the spoon with a dry towel and check the towel. If your child felt wetness and the towel stays dry, the cold may explain the feeling. A damp spot can come from condensation.

scenes.tts: Ask your child to close their eyes. Brush a craft feather over a fingertip, the back of the hand, an elbow, and a foot. Ask where they felt it best. Then label five cards for eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin. Sort the describing words together.
scenes.caption: Ask your child to close their eyes. Brush a craft feather over a fingertip, the back of the hand, an elbow, and a foot. Ask where they felt it best. Then label five cards for eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin. Sort the describing words together.
scenes.visual: Show the craft feather brushing a fingertip, the back of the hand, an elbow, and a foot in sequence. Return to the table. Match one word card at a time to an eye, an ear, a nose, a tongue, or skin.
scenes.narration: Ask your child to close their eyes. Brush a craft feather over a fingertip, the back of the hand, an elbow, and a foot. Ask where they felt it best. Then label five cards for eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin. Sort the describing words together.

scenes.tts: Stay with your child the whole time. Keep small things like marbles, beads, coins, batteries, and magnets away from children under four. Call nine one one if a child is choking.
scenes.caption: Stay with your child the whole time. Keep small things like marbles, beads, coins, batteries, and magnets away from children under four. Call nine one one if a child is choking.
scenes.visual: Same table. Up to three clear badges: adult and child side by side ('Stay together'), a crossed-out marble, coin and battery labeled 'Under 4: choking risk', and a phone icon ('Choking: call 911').
scenes.narration: Stay with your child the whole time. Keep small things like marbles, beads, coins, batteries, and magnets away from children under four. Call nine one one if a child is choking.

scenes.tts: Check for allergies first, and leave out balloons and rubber gloves if anyone has a latex allergy. Use a craft-store feather. Everyone washes hands afterward.
scenes.caption: Check for allergies first, and leave out balloons and rubber gloves if anyone has a latex allergy. Use a craft-store feather. Everyone washes hands afterward.
scenes.visual: Badges swap: a crossed-out balloon and glove labeled 'Latex allergy?', a craft feather with a store tag, and soapy hands.
scenes.narration: Check for allergies first, and leave out balloons and rubber gloves if anyone has a latex allergy. Use a craft-store feather. Everyone washes hands afterward.

scenes.tts: End by asking, 'What could your hand tell you about the orange? What could only your eyes tell you?' Skin found shape, texture, and cold. Eyes found color.
scenes.caption: End by asking, 'What could your hand tell you about the orange? What could only your eyes tell you?' Skin found shape, texture, and cold. Eyes found color.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full table: the bag, the orange, the two spoons and the sorted word cards in their places. The hand column and eye column from earlier glow once.
scenes.narration: End by asking, 'What could your hand tell you about the orange? What could only your eyes tell you?' Skin found shape, texture, and cold. Eyes found color.

scenes.line: Touch finds shape, texture and cold, but not color.
scenes.visual: Clean warm end card with a faint pillowcase in the background. Centered, large, high-contrast text: 'Touch finds shape, texture and cold, but not color.'
